title: The commit-msg hook prints that check-trailers refuses a stray KB-Work line but lets the commit through
goal: kg_trailers.refuse_commit_msg gives the verdict check-trailers gives for a KB-Work line outside the message's last paragraph (a stray line git does not read as a trailer): REFUSED where check-trailers refuses the commit, so the hook never prints 'refuses this commit' and exits 0, and kb/_self/git.md says what the hook does with such a line. Found by the SP-kbrxa4c4 review (S3, ST-3mfjrjom).

run:
import os,sys,tempfile
sys.path.insert(0,'_tools')
import kg_trailers as k
f=tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w',delete=False,suffix='.txt');f.write('feat: x\n\nKB-Work: ST-cccccccc\n\nbody\n');f.close()
r=k.refuse_commit_msg(f.name,None);os.unlink(f.name)
print('stray KB-Work line refused',r==k.REFUSED);sys.exit(0 if r==k.REFUSED else 1)

notes:
Review 2026-10-18: in a scratch repo with the hook, `git commit -m $'feat: x

KB-Work: ST-cccccccc

body'` returns 0, then `python3 _tools/kbgit.py check-trailers HEAD` returns 1.
